entries.claim: Adding `lanternFlicker` as ordinary prose removes the fixture's structural-only match and weakens the test that distinguishes entity matching from textual mention.
entries.failure_scenario: If extraction or querying of the `Edit` tool's path/old-string entities regresses completely, a query for `lanternFlicker` can still find this turn through the newly added text block, so the structural-match assertion passes without proving structural matching works. This also contradicts the fixture documentation that the turn keeps “matched structurally” and “mentions the words” as different answers.

counter_evidence.note: Entities come only from structured tool records, so the added text block emits none; the structural-versus-prose distinction this fixture keeps is between the Edit turn and the third, prose-only turn naming lantern.rs, which is unchanged. The prompt-arm tests that read this fixture prompt by the path and inject only on a structural match (crates/terminus-core/src/inject/prompt.rs:30), so a text-only reach of lanternFlicker is never eligible and cannot make them pass.

entries.claim: The `edits` helper now places the structural target `beaconWaver` in plain text, so tests using it can no longer prove that the prompt arm reached the turn structurally.
entries.failure_scenario: A regression that stops indexing or matching the `Edit` tool's path/entity still leaves `beaconWaver` available to text scoring in the preceding text block. Suppression or injection tests can therefore continue passing via a prose match while the structural retrieval path they purport to cover is broken.

counter_evidence.note: The prompt arm never injects a hit the query reached only through its text, whatever its relevance; a hit needs a stored entity in the top three or two co-occurring entities. With structural matching broken, beaconWaver in the prose block gives a text-only hit, which is ineligible, so the suppression tests that expect an injection would fail rather than pass.
